1:6.headline: Riphath in Genesis becomes Diphath here: weak at first, then blemished
1:6.body: Genesis spells this name with a resh, ריפת. Here it has a dalet, דיפת. Rashi reads both: at first these people were רפין, "weak", and at the end they were full of דופי, "blemish". Radak says only that the two letters look alike.

sources.quote: שֶׁמִּתְּחִלָּה הָיוּ רָפִין וְלֹא הָיוּ מִתְגַּבְּרִים עַל יִשְׂרָאֵל, וְלַסּוֹף נִתְמַלְּאוּ דּוֹפִי וְרִיעוּעַ
sources.says: Rashi says at first they were weak and did not overpower Israel, and in the end they were full of blemish and decay.

sources.quote: ובתורה כתיב וריפת ברי״ש ובשתי השמות היה נקרא
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the Torah spells it with a resh, and he was called by both names.

sources.quote: ולפי שהדל"ת והרי"ש קרובים בכתיבתם
sources.says: Radak says dalet and resh look alike in writing, so readers of old records read the names both ways.

1:7.headline: Dodanim or Rodanim: cousins when Israel is strong, rulers when it sins
1:7.body: Genesis calls this people דודנים, Dodanim. Here they are רודנים, Rodanim. Rashi, after Genesis Rabbah, hears both: when Israel sins they come and rule (רודים) over it, and when Israel is strong they say "you are our cousins" (דודינו).

sources.quote: כְּשֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל חוֹטְאִים הֵם בָּאִים וְרוֹדִים בָּהֶם, וּכְשֶׁיַּד יִשְׂרָאֵל תַּקִּיפָה הֵם אוֹמְרִים: בְּנֵי דוֹדֵינוּ אַתֶּם
sources.says: Rashi says that when Israel sins they come and rule over them, and when Israel is strong they say "you are our cousins".

sources.quote: נכתב בספר בראשית באחד מן הקריאות ונכתב בספר הזה באחרת, להודיע כי הכל שם אחד
sources.says: Radak says Genesis wrote one reading and this book wrote the other, to show it is all one name.

1:10.headline: Nimrod, the name that sounds like "rebel"
1:10.body: The Targum says Nimrod began to be mighty in sin, shed innocent blood and rebelled (מרד) against God. Malbim notes that Rashi on Genesis follows this midrash: Nimrod led the world to rebel against God.

sources.quote: הוּא שָׁרֵי לְמֶהֱוֵי גִבָּר בַּחֲטָאָה שְׁדִי אֲדַם זַכַּאי וּמְרוֹד קֳדָם יְיָ
sources.says: The Targum says he began to be mighty in sin, shed innocent blood and rebelled before the Lord.

sources.quote: ובפי' התורה (בראשית י, ח) כתב רש"י כפי הדרש שהמריד את העולם על השי"ת
sources.says: Malbim says Rashi on Genesis follows the midrash that Nimrod made the world rebel against God.

1:19.headline: Peleg, "split", because in his days the earth was divided
1:19.body: The verse explains the name itself: in Peleg's days the earth נפלגה, "was split". Metzudat David says people split apart over the earth. Rashi says human lifespans were split in half. Malbim says the other peoples split away from Peleg's language.

sources.quote: בני הארץ נפרדו זה מזה ע״פ כל האדמה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the people of the earth separated from one another across the land.

sources.quote: נִתְחַלְּקוּ וְנִתְמַעֲטוּ יְמֵיהֶם שֶׁל בְּרִיּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says the lifespans of people were divided and grew shorter.

sources.quote: ולכן נקרא הוא פלג, שכולם נפלגו ממנו בלשונם
sources.says: Malbim says he was called Peleg because everyone split off from him in their language.

1:20.headline: Almodad, the one who measured the earth
1:20.body: The Targum turns this name into a deed. It hears מדד, "measure", in it: Almodad measured out the earth with ropes.

sources.quote: וּפַלְגוּת אַרְעָא בְּאוּשְׁלַיָא
sources.says: The Targum says Almodad measured the divisions of the earth with ropes.

1:20.headline: Sheleph, the one who drew off the rivers
1:20.body: שלף means "to draw out", in Aramaic as in Hebrew. The Targum reads the name this way: Sheleph drew off the rivers to the borders.

sources.quote: דִשְׁלַף יַת נְהַרְוָתָא לִתְחוּמַיָא
sources.says: The Targum says Sheleph drew off the rivers to the borders.

1:27.headline: Abram is Abraham, "father of a multitude of nations"
1:27.body: The verse gives both names. Radak and Metzudat David say Abraham means "father of a multitude of nations". Malbim adds that the sages forbid calling him Abram, so the verse says "that is Abraham".

sources.quote: הוא הנקרא אחר זה בשם אברהם ע״ש אב המון גוים
sources.says: Metzudat David says he was later called Abraham, after "father of a multitude of nations".

sources.quote: שאהבו השם וגדל שמו כי אב המון גוים נתנו
sources.says: Radak says God loved him and made his name great, setting him as father of a multitude of nations.

sources.quote: וכל הקורא לאברהם אברם עובר בעשה
sources.says: Malbim says that whoever calls Abraham "Abram" breaks a commandment, citing Berakhot 13a.

1:30.headline: Hear, be silent, bear: the Targum translates the names
1:30.body: The Targum does not keep these names of Ishmael's sons. It translates them. משמע, Mishma, becomes "listening", דומה, Dumah, becomes "silence", and משא, Massa, becomes "bearing".

sources.quote: וְצָיְתָא וּשְׁתוֹקָא וּמְסוֹבָרָא
sources.says: The Targum renders Mishma, Dumah and Massa as "listening", "silence" and "bearing".

1:32.headline: Keturah was "only" a concubine, and the verse says so
1:32.body: Genesis says Abraham "took a wife", Keturah. Here she is called a concubine. Radak says Sarah was his only wife. Rashi says the book tells every lowly fact about these sons, for the honor of Isaac.

sources.quote: כי לא היתה לו אשה אלא שרה אמנו, והשאר פלגשים
sources.says: Radak says Abraham had no wife but Sarah; the others were concubines.

sources.quote: כָּל גְּנַאי שֶׁיָּכוֹל לְסַפֵּר בָּהֶם, הוּא מְסַפֵּר, מִשּׁוּם כְּבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל יִצְחָק
sources.says: Rashi says the book tells every shame it can about them, for the honor of Isaac.

1:36.headline: Is Timna a son of Eliphaz, or his concubine?
1:36.body: Here Timna is listed among Eliphaz's sons. Genesis says Timna was his concubine. Radak reports a midrash that Timna was his daughter, later his concubine. Malbim suggests this Timna is a man, Korah, known by two names.

sources.quote: הנראה מן הפסוק הזה כי תמנע הוא בן אליפז, ובתורה כת' כי תמנע היתה פלגש לאליפז
sources.says: Radak says this verse makes Timna look like a son of Eliphaz, while the Torah says Timna was his concubine.

sources.quote: שאף היא היתה בתו, ואחר כן היתה לו פלגש וילדה לו עמלק
sources.says: Radak reports the view that she was also his daughter, and later became his concubine and bore him Amalek.

sources.quote: וקרח זה נקרא בשני שמות, שאמו קראתו בשם קרח, ואליפז קרא שמו תמנע
sources.says: Malbim says Korah had two names: his mother called him Korah and Eliphaz called him Timna.

1:41.headline: From Hemdan, "desirable", to Hamran, like a donkey
1:41.body: Genesis calls him חמדן, Hemdan. Here he is חמרן, Hamran. Rashi hears both: at first they were desirable (חמודים) like the righteous, and in the end ugly like a donkey (חמור).

sources.quote: בִּתְחִלָּה הָיוּ חֲמוּדִים וְנֶחֱמָדִין כַּצַּדִּיקִים, וּלְבַסּוֹף מְכֻעָרִין כַּחֲמוֹר
sources.says: Rashi says at first they were desirable like the righteous, and in the end ugly like a donkey.

sources.quote: ובני דישון חמרן – ברי"ש, ובתורה "חמדן" (בר' לו,כו) בדל'
sources.says: Radak notes the name is spelled with a resh here and with a dalet in the Torah.

1:43.headline: The Targum says the first king of Edom was Balaam
1:43.body: The verse names Bela son of Beor. The Targum says this is Balaam son of Beor, the wicked, and that he is Laban the Aramean, who joined Esau's sons to destroy Jacob.

sources.quote: בִּלְעָם בַּר בְּעוֹר רַשִׁיעָא הוּא לָבָן אֲרָמָאָה
sources.says: The Targum says he is Balaam son of Beor the wicked, who is Laban the Aramean.

sources.quote: וּמִית בָּלַע דְקַטְלֵיהּ פִּנְחָס בְּמַדְבְּרָא
sources.says: The Targum says Bela died, killed by Pinchas in the wilderness.

1:50.headline: Me-Zahav, "what is gold?"
1:50.body: Metzudat David and Ralbag read מי זהב as a man's name. The Targum reads מי זהב as a question, "what is gold?" It tells of one who grew rich, became proud, and said "what is silver, what is gold?"

sources.quote: וּמִן דַעֲתַר וּקְנָא נִכְסִין הֲוָה מִתְגָאָה וַהֲדַר לְמֵימַר מָה הוּא כַּסְפָּא וּמָה הוּא דַהֲבָא
sources.says: The Targum says that once rich, he grew proud and said "what is silver and what is gold?"

sources.quote: מטרד היתה בת מי זהב והוא שם אדם
sources.says: Metzudat David says Matred was the daughter of Me-Zahav, which is a person's name.

sources.quote: והיא היתה בת איש שמו מי זהב
sources.says: Ralbag says she was the daughter of a man named Me-Zahav.

12:2.headline: 'Right-handing and left-handing': they could shoot with either hand
12:2.body: מימינים ומשמאלים are rare verbs made from 'right' and 'left'. Radak and Metzudat David say these archers could shoot stones and arrows with both hands. Malbim adds that many men of Benjamin were left-handed.

sources.quote: שהיו שולטים בשתי ידיהם בין לירות אבנים בין לירות חיצים
sources.says: Radak says they had full use of both hands, to shoot stones or arrows.

sources.quote: שולטים בשתי ידיהם לירות באבנים ובחצים
sources.says: Metzudat David says they could use both hands to shoot stones and arrows with the bow.

sources.quote: כי רוב בני בנימין היו אטר יד ימין
sources.says: Malbim says most men of Benjamin were left-handed, pointing to Judges 20:16.

12:2.headline: Stones shot from a bow, which Rashi says he saw often
12:2.body: The verse says these archers shot stones as well as arrows. Rashi explains they set a stone on the bowstring. He adds that he had seen this done many times.

sources.quote: הָיוּ נוֹתְנִים עַל יֶתֶר הַקֶּשֶׁת אֶבֶן מוֹרִים. וַאֲנִי רָאִיתִי כֵן הַרְבֵּה
sources.says: Rashi says they put a stone on the bowstring and shot it, and that he himself saw this often.

12:4.headline: 'The thirty': a band of thirty heroes, or simply the officers?
12:4.body: Ralbag reads בשלשים as the thirty famous heroes listed in the book of Samuel. Metzudat Zion reads it as 'officers', from the same root as Pharaoh's chosen שלישיו in the Song at the Sea.

sources.quote: ר"ל בשלשים הגבורים הנזכרים בראשונה שהם נזכרים גם כן בספר שמואל
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the thirty heroes listed earlier, who also appear in the book of Samuel.

sources.quote: בשרים כמו ומבחר שלישיו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means 'among the officers', as in 'his chosen officers'.

12:16.headline: Did they chase off the valley people, or lay beams across the deeps?
12:16.body: ויבריחו can come from ברח, to flee, or from בריח, a beam. Radak says the people of the valleys fled. Ralbag says the soldiers laid beams over the deep parts of the flooded Jordan. Rashi says they split the deep waters with their shields and crossed on dry land.

sources.quote: הבריחו יושבי העמקים בעברם צבא גדול, וחשבו כי אויבים היו וברחו
sources.says: Radak says the valley dwellers saw a great army crossing, took them for enemies, and fled.

sources.quote: שכל המקומות שהיו עמוקים בנהר ההוא שמו בהם בריחים לעבור עליהם
sources.says: Ralbag says they set beams in all the deep places of the river so they could cross.

sources.quote: וּבָקְעוּ בְּמָגִנֵּיהֶם אֶת כָּל עִמְקֵי הַמַּיִם לַמִּזְרָח וְלַמַּעֲרָב, וְעָבְרוּ בַּיַּבָּשָׁה
sources.says: Rashi says they split all the deep waters with their shields and crossed on dry land, and also gives the reading about the valley peoples.

2:2.headline: Dan is listed before Joseph, out of order
2:2.body: Malbim says Dan comes before Joseph here, as in one other list. A midrash says Joseph and Benjamin were born because of Dan's merit.

sources.quote: קדימת דן ליוסף נמצא עוד פעם אחד בסדר מסעי, וחז"ל אמרו במדרש מפני שבזכות דן נולד יוסף ובנימין
sources.says: Malbim says Dan before Joseph appears once more, in the portion Masei, and the sages said in a midrash that Joseph and Benjamin were born in Dan's merit.

2:3.headline: Judah's wife: a real Canaanite, or a merchant's daughter?
2:3.body: Genesis calls her father "a Canaanite man". The midrash reads "Canaanite" as "merchant". Malbim says this verse shows he was a true Canaanite.

sources.quote: מבואר שמ"ש (בראשית לח, ב) בת איש כנעני אין פירושו תגר רק כנעני ממש
sources.says: Malbim says "daughter of a Canaanite man" in Genesis 38 does not mean "merchant" but a real Canaanite, and he notes that the midrash reads it as merchant.

2:6.headline: The wise "Ezrahites" of Kings are Zerach's sons
2:6.body: Kings says Solomon was wiser than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol and Darda. Rashi says the extra alef in אזרחי means it is the same as "of Zerach", so these are the sons of Zerach named here.

sources.quote: וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר ״הָאֶזְרָחִי״ – אָלֶ״ף יְתֵיר, כְּמוֹ ״הַזַּרְחִי״ (במדבר כו:יג), מִזֶּרַח יָצָא
sources.says: Rashi says the "Ezrahite" in Kings has an extra alef, like "the Zarchi" in Numbers, meaning he came from Zerach.

2:7.headline: Achan is called Achar, "troubler", for the trouble he caused
2:7.body: Joshua calls him Achan. Here he is Achar, which sounds like the word for "trouble". The commentators say the name was changed on purpose, because he brought trouble on Israel.

sources.quote: וְלָמָּה אֲנִי קוֹרֵהוּ עָכָר, וַהֲלֹא עָכָן שְׁמוֹ? (וּמְפֹרָָשׁ) לְפִי שֶׁהוּא עָכַר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעָבַר עַל הַחֵרֶם
sources.says: Rashi asks why he is called Achar when his name was Achan, and answers that he troubled Israel by breaking the ban.

sources.quote: ועכר הוא עכן, אלא שקראו "עכר" לגנאי כי עכר ישראל
sources.says: Radak says Achar is Achan, called Achar as a shame because he troubled Israel.

sources.quote: עוכר. ענין בלבול והשחתה כמו עכרתם אותי (בראשית לד)
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says עוכר means confusion and ruin, like "you have troubled me" in Genesis 34.

sources.quote: וקראו אותו עכר ע"ש שעכר את ישראל, שהרי"ש והנו"ן מתחלף בשמות, כמו נבוכדנצר נבוכדרצר
sources.says: Malbim says he was called Achar after he troubled Israel, since the letters resh and nun swap in names, as in Nebuchadnezzar and Nebuchadrezzar.

2:11.headline: The sages say Boaz is the judge Ibzan
2:11.body: Rashi says the sages call Boaz by the name Ibzan, from Judges 12:8. He is amazed at the dates, which would make Boaz about 300 years old, and answers with Ruth 4:13, where the Lord "gave her conception".

sources.quote: רַבּוֹתֵינוּ אָמְרוּ ״אַבְצָן״ (שופטים יב:ח) זֶה בֹּעַז
sources.says: Rashi says our rabbis said that "Ivtzan" in Judges is Boaz.

sources.quote: וְאֵיךְ הוֹלִיד בֹּעַז בֶּן שְׁלוֹשׁ מֵאוֹת שָׁנָה: וְיֶשׁ לוֹמַר: עַל כֵּן אָמַר (רות ד:יג): ״וַיִּתֵּן ה׳ לָהּ הֵרָיוֹן״
sources.says: Rashi asks how Boaz could have fathered a child at three hundred years, and answers that Ruth 4:13 says "the Lord gave her conception".

2:13.headline: Jesse is spelled with an alef, which hints at "a mighty man"
2:13.body: Here Jesse is written ואישי, with an alef. Rashi says the full spelling points to "a man of strength", as in Ruth 2:1. Radak says it is only a swap among the letters alef, he, vav and yod.

sources.quote: וְאִישַׁי הוֹלִיד אֶת בְּכֹרוֹ. מָלֵא אָלֶ״ף, כְּלוֹמַר: אִישׁ גִּבּוֹר חַיִל (רות ב:א)
sources.says: Rashi says the name is spelled full with an alef, meaning a man of strength and valor, as in Ruth 2:1.

sources.quote: ואישי הוליד. באל"ף וביו"ד אחד, כי אותיות אהו"י מתחלפות
sources.says: Radak says it is written with an alef and one yod, because the letters alef, he, vav and yod interchange.

2:15.headline: David is "the seventh" here, but Samuel counts eight sons
2:15.body: First Samuel says Jesse had eight sons, with David the youngest. Rashi says the eighth, Elihu, is skipped because the list has reached David, "the pearl". Radak says this verse counts only the sons of David's own mother.

sources.quote: וְעַתָּה מָצָא הַמַּרְגָּלִית, לְפִיכָךְ לֹא מָנָה הַשְּׁמִינִי: ״אֱלִיהוּ״ (דה״א כז:יח)
sources.says: Rashi says David has now found the pearl, so the list does not count the eighth, Elihu.

sources.quote: ובכאן זכר השבעה שהיו מאם אחת עם דוד
sources.says: Radak says that here the book names the seven who were from one mother with David.

sources.quote: דויד השביעי. ולא זכר השמיני שהוא אליהו
sources.says: Metzudat David says the book does not name the eighth, who is Elihu.

2:17.headline: Jether is an "Ishmaelite" here and an "Israelite" in Samuel
2:17.body: Rashi and Radak say he is the same man, called Ishmaelite because he lived in the land of Ishmael. Radak adds that Samuel calls him Israelite so no one thinks he came from Ishmael's line.

sources.quote: וּבִשְׁמוּאֵל (שמואל ב יז:כה) כָּתוּב ״הַיִּשְׂרְאֵלִי״! בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׁמָעֵאל הָיָה דָּר
sources.says: Rashi says Samuel writes "the Israelite", and that here he is called Ishmaelite because he lived in the land of Ishmael.

sources.quote: ולפיכך קראו "ישראלי", שלא יחשב אדם לפי שקראו "ישמעאלי" שהיה מזרע ישמעאל – אלא מזרע ישראל היה
sources.says: Radak says he was called "Israelite" elsewhere so that no one would think "Ishmaelite" meant he came from Ishmael's seed, since he came from Israel's.

sources.quote: וי"ל שהיה גר ישמעאלי ואחר שנתגייר שינו שמו מיתר ליתרא, וקראוהו ישראלי
sources.says: Malbim suggests he was an Ishmaelite convert whose name was changed from Jether to Jithra and who was then called Israelite.

2:18.headline: Did Caleb father his wives? It depends on the word את
2:18.body: Plainly the verse says Caleb "fathered Azubah, a wife". Radak and Metzudat David read את as "from", so he had children from his wife Azubah. Rashi says Azubah-Ishah was his daughter, named after his wife.

sources.quote: הוליד בנים מן עזובה אשתו ומן יריעות וכן כצאתי את העיר (שמות ט׳:כ״ט) ומשפטו מן העיר
sources.says: Metzudat David says he fathered sons from his wife Azubah and from Jerioth, and that את here means "from", as in "when I leave the city" in Exodus 9.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי כי "את" זה כמו "מן", וכן "כצאתי את העיר" (שמ' ט,כט)
sources.says: Radak says that in his view this את means "from", as in "when I leave the city".

sources.quote: לְפִי שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ אִשָּׁה שֶׁשְּׁמָהּ עֲזוּבָה, לְכָךְ כִּנָּה אֶת שֵׁם בִּתּוֹ עֲזוּבָה אִשָּׁה
sources.says: Rashi says Caleb had a wife named Azubah, so he named his daughter "Azubah Ishah".

2:20.headline: Bezalel's family tree fits only if each father was under eight
2:20.body: Caleb was forty when he was sent as a spy, and Bezalel had already built the Tabernacle by then. Rashi counts the years and says each father in the line was under eight when his son was born.

sources.quote: צֵא וַחֲשׁוֹב, שֶׁכָּל אֶחָד מֵהֶם הָיָה פָּחוֹת מִן שְׁמוֹנֶה שָׁנִים כְּשֶׁהוֹלִידוּ
sources.says: Rashi says to work it out: each of them was less than eight years old when he fathered his son.

2:22.headline: Is this the Jair of the Torah? Radak and the sages differ
2:22.body: Radak says yes: the Torah calls him a son of Manasseh because his father's mother was Machir's daughter. The sages say no: this Jair married a woman from Gilead and inherited her cities.

sources.quote: ומה שאמ' בתורה "בן מנשה" (שם) – ממשפחת האם, כי אם אביו היתה בת מכיר בן מנשה
sources.says: Radak says "son of Manasseh" in the Torah comes through the mother's family, since his father's mother was a daughter of Machir son of Manasseh.

sources.quote: ארז״ל שלקח אשה מארץ הגלעד וממנה ירש הערים האלה ואין זה יאיר הכתוב בתורה
sources.says: Metzudat David says the sages said he took a wife from Gilead and inherited these cities from her, and this is not the Jair of the Torah.

2:24.headline: "Caleb-Ephrathah": a place named for them, or a time?
2:24.body: Rashi says Caleb-Ephrathah is a city named for Caleb's wife Ephrath. Radak gives that view too, but prefers "when Caleb took Ephrath as his wife, Hezron died".

sources.quote: עַל שֵׁם (כָָָָּלֵב) אִשְׁתּוֹ קָרְאוּ אֶת הָעִיר (כָָּלֵב) אֶפְרָתָה
sources.says: Rashi says the city was called Caleb-Ephrathah after his wife.

sources.quote: ולפי דעתי כי פרושו: בעת שלקח כלב בנו אפרתה אשתו, באותה העת מת חצרון
sources.says: Radak says that in his view it means: at the time Caleb his son took Ephrath as his wife, Hezron died.

2:26.headline: Why "Atarah"? The sages read it as adorning himself with her
2:26.body: Her name sounds like "crown". The Jerusalem Talmud, as Rashi and Radak report it, says Jerahmeel took a foreign woman "to adorn himself with her", and Radak adds she was a daughter of great people.

sources.quote: וּבִיבָמוֹת יְרוּשַׁלְמִי כָּתַב (ירושלמי סנהדרין ב:ג) שֶׁלָּקַח נָכְרִית לְהִתְעַטֵּר בָּהּ יָפֶה
sources.says: Rashi says the Jerusalem Talmud writes that he took a foreign woman to adorn himself beautifully with her.

sources.quote: לכך הזכיר "ושמה עטרה" – שלקחה להתעטר בה, כי בת גדולים היתה
sources.says: Radak says that is why the verse mentions her name Atarah: he took her to adorn himself with her, since she was a daughter of great people.

sources.quote: ושמה עטרה שלקחה להתעטר בה שהיתה יפת תואר
sources.says: Malbim says her name was Atarah because he took her to adorn himself with her, since she was beautiful.

2:34.headline: Sheshan had no sons, yet verse 31 names his son
2:34.body: Verse 31 says "the sons of Sheshan: Ahlai", but here Sheshan had only daughters. Rashi and Radak say Ahlai died without children, and Ralbag suggests Ahlai was a daughter.

sources.quote: וּמַה שֶּׁאָמַר לְמַעְלָה ״וּבְנֵי שֵׁשָׁן אַחְלָי״ (דברי הימים א ב:לא) – חוֹלֶה שָׁפָל הָיָה, וּמֵת בְּלֹא בָנִים
sources.says: Rashi says Ahlai, named above, was sick and low, and died without children.

sources.quote: אלא שמת אחלי בחיי אביו, ולא נשאר ממנו לא בן ולא בת
sources.says: Radak says Ahlai died in his father's lifetime and left neither son nor daughter.

sources.quote: ידמה שמה שאמר ובני ששן אחלי היה שם בת היתה לו ואמר ובני על אחד במספר כמו שאמר ובני דן חושים
sources.says: Ralbag says it seems Ahlai was the name of a daughter, and the verse said "sons" for one, as in "the sons of Dan: Hushim".

2:34.headline: Yarcha's name hides "a freed servant", read backwards
2:34.body: Yarcha was Sheshan's Egyptian servant, who married his daughter. Radak gives a midrash that splits the name: ע stands for "servant" and ירח reversed is חרי, "free", so the name shows Sheshan freed him.

sources.quote: ודרך דרש כי מן השם למדו שעשאו בן חורין, כי "ירחע" – "עבד חרי": העי"ן – "עבד", ו"ירח" – "חרי" בהפך
sources.says: Radak says a midrash learns from the name that Sheshan freed him, reading ירחע as "avad chari": the ע is "servant" and ירח is "chari" reversed.

2:48.headline: "Begot" is the male form, though Maacah is a woman
2:48.body: The verse says Caleb's concubine Maacah "begot" Sheber, using the male verb. Radak and Metzudat David say the verb belongs to Caleb: he fathered Sheber by her. Malbim finds that forced and reads it another way.

sources.quote: פילגש כלב מעכה ילד. "ילד" אינו חוזר למעכה, כי היה אומ' "ילדה", אלא לכלב
sources.says: Radak says "yalad" does not refer back to Maacah, since it would then say "yaldah", but to Caleb.

sources.quote: ילד שבר. רצה לומר כלב ילד ממנה את שבר וכו׳
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means Caleb fathered Sheber by her.

sources.quote: המפ' נדחקו מאד, ולדבריהם בא ילד תחת ילדה
sources.says: Malbim says the commentators were greatly strained, and that on their view "yalad" stands in place of "yaldah".

2:52.headline: A puzzling phrase: a title, a place, or two names?
2:52.body: "The seer, half of the Menuchoth" is read several ways. Rashi says he governed half of a province called Menuchot. Radak lists other readings and prefers that these are two sons' names, Haroeh and Chatzi-ha-Menuchot.

sources.quote: מְדִינָה אַחַת הָיְתָה בָּאָרֶץ וּמְנוּחוֹת שְׁמָהּ, דִּכְתִיב ״וַיַּגְלֵם אֶל מָנַחַת״ (דברי הימים א ח:ו); וְהוּא הַמּוֹשֵׁל עַל חֲצִי מְדִינָה
sources.says: Rashi says there was a province in the land called Menuchot, and he is the ruler over half the province.

sources.quote: ויש מפרשים שהיה רואה וממונה על חצי המנחות הבאות לירושלים מאת כל הגוים
sources.says: Radak lists a reading that he oversaw half of the offerings brought to Jerusalem from all the nations.

sources.quote: והנראה בעיני כי "הרואה חצי המנחות" הם שמות בני שובל, בנים אחרים לבד אשר ישבו בקרית יערים
sources.says: Radak says that in his view "the seer, half of the Menuchoth" are names of Shobal's other sons, who lived in Kiriath-jearim.

sources.quote: שם האחד הרואה ושם האחד חצי המנוחות
sources.says: Metzudat David says one name is Haroeh and the other is Chatzi-ha-Menuchot.

2:55.headline: Rashi reads "Kenites" as smiths, from the Aramaic
2:55.body: Rashi says הקינים means refiners of metal, because the Aramaic translation of "goldsmith" in Judges 17 is קינאה. Radak adds that the sages said they were descendants of Moses' father-in-law, who joined the families of Judah.

sources.quote: צוֹרְפִים, ״וַיִּתְּנֵהוּ לַצּוֹרֵף״ (שופטים יז:ד) – תַּרְגּוּמוֹ: ״לְקִינָאָה״ (תרגום יונתן)
sources.says: Rashi says הקינים means refiners, as in "and he gave it to the refiner" in Judges 17, which Targum Jonathan renders "to the kinaah".

sources.quote: אמרו כי הם מבני קיני חותן משה, ונתערבו במשפחות יהודה ונתיחשו עמם
sources.says: Radak says the sages said they come from the sons of the Kenite, Moses' father-in-law, and mixed into the families of Judah and were counted with them.

20:2.headline: The crown of their king, or of their idol Milcom?
20:2.body: מלכם can mean "their king". Metzudat Zion says it may also be מלכום, the god of Ammon, so the crown was taken from the idol.

sources.quote: מלכם. העבודת כוכבים הקרויה מלכום או כפשוטו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the idol called Milcom, or else the plain meaning, their king.

20:5.headline: A spear like a weaver's beam
20:5.body: מנור is the round wooden beam a weaver winds the threads on. Rashi brings the sages: David, whose mother wove curtains for the Temple on such a beam, would defeat the giant whose spear was like one.

sources.quote: הוא העץ העגול אשר האורג כורך בו חוטי השתי
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it is the round beam the weaver winds the threads on.

sources.quote: יָבֹא דָּוִד שֶׁאִמּוֹ אוֹרֶגֶת פָּרוֹכֶת לְבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בִּמְנוֹר אוֹרְגִים, וְיַהֲרֹג אֶת גָּלְיַת שֶׁעֵץ חֲנִיתוֹ כִּמְנוֹר אוֹרְגִים
sources.says: Rashi says, measure for measure, David, whose mother wove Temple curtains on a weaver's beam, would kill Goliath, whose spear was like a weaver's beam.

26:7.headline: 'His brothers', or a son named Achiv?
26:7.body: The words אחיו בני חיל look like 'his brothers, strong men'. Metzudat David says they are two more names: one son was called Achiv and another Bnei Chayil.

sources.quote: כן שמות בניו האחד אחיו והשני בני חיל
sources.says: Metzudat David says these are the names of his sons: one was Achiv and the other Bnei Chayil.

26:8.headline: A man of chayil: not a soldier but a respected man
26:8.body: חיל often means strength or an army. Rashi says here it means neither. It means a man of standing, the way Boaz is described in Ruth.

sources.quote: לֹא בְּכֹחַ וְלֹא בְּמִלְחָמָה, אֶלָּא כְּאָדָם שֶׁאוֹמֵר עָלָיו פְּלוֹנִי חָשׁוּב
sources.says: Rashi says it is not about strength or war, but like saying of someone that he is an important man.

26:8.headline: Sixty-two here, sixty-eight before: why the count differs
26:8.body: Chapter 16 counts sixty-eight for Oved-Edom, but here it is sixty-two. Metzudat David suggests six had died by David's old age. Radak suggests the earlier count included Oved-Edom's six brothers.

sources.quote: ולמעלה נאמר ששים ושמונה ואולי מתו ששה לעת זקנת דוד
sources.says: Metzudat David says earlier it said sixty-eight, and perhaps six died by the time David was old.

sources.quote: אפשר כי היו לעובד אדום ששה אחים, ועם אותם היו כלם ששים ושמנה
sources.says: Radak says Oved-Edom may have had six brothers, and with them they were sixty-eight.

26:14.headline: Zechariah: a wise adviser, or a man who chose wisely?
26:14.body: Metzudat David reads יועץ בשכל as a title: a man of wise counsel. Malbim reads it as something Zechariah did. He wisely gave up his place at the east gate so no one else would be shamed, and then drew the north.

sources.quote: שהיה בעל עצה בהשכל רב
sources.says: Metzudat David says he was a man of counsel with great understanding.

sources.quote: וקבל עליו לדחות ממקומו, שאם ידחה אחר יהיה לו בושה
sources.says: Malbim says Zechariah agreed to be moved from his place, since if someone else were moved it would shame him.

26:16.headline: Shuppim: a man, or the gate by the rubbish heap?
26:16.body: Metzudat David thinks שפים is a person, perhaps listed earlier under another name. Malbim reads it as a place, from אשפה, refuse: where trash was thrown out. He says it is the same spot later called פרבר.

sources.quote: אולי נזכר למעלה בשמו האחר
sources.says: Metzudat David says he was perhaps mentioned earlier by his other name.

sources.quote: ונקרא שפים מל' אשפה, והוא עצמו המקום שקורא בפי"ח פרבר
sources.says: Malbim says it is called Shuppim from ashpah, refuse, and it is the same place verse 18 calls Parbar.

26:18.headline: Parbar: the spot toward the outside
26:18.body: Rashi brings the Talmud's reading: לפרבר means כלפי בר, 'toward the outside'. Malbim hears אפר בר: the place where ashes were carried out. Metzudat David says it is the name of a room.

sources.quote: אָמַר רָבָא: לַפַּרְבָּר כְּלַפֵּי בָּר
sources.says: Rashi cites Rava in the Talmud that laparbar means 'toward the outside'.

sources.quote: אפר בר. ששם היו משליכים את האפר לחוץ
sources.says: Malbim reads it as 'ash outside', since there they threw the ash out.

sources.quote: והוא שם חדר מה
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the name of some room.

26:29.headline: The 'outside work': in the forests, or among the people?
26:29.body: Rashi and Radak say the outside work was done outside the city: cutting cedars, cutting stone, and farming Temple fields. Ralbag says it was Temple business out among the people, like collecting the half-shekel each year.

sources.quote: מְלָאכָה שֶׁעוֹשִׂין חוּץ לָעִיר בַּיְּעָרִים וּבֶהָרִים
sources.says: Rashi says it is work done outside the city, in forests and mountains.

sources.quote: המלאכה שהיתה חוץ לעיר, לחטב עצים ביערות ולחצב אבנים
sources.says: Radak says it is work outside the city: cutting wood in forests and cutting stone.

sources.quote: להישירם לפרוע מחצית השקל שנה בשנה
sources.says: Ralbag says it was guiding the people to pay the half-shekel each year.

26:30.headline: 'Beyond the Jordan, westward': which side is that?
26:30.body: Land beyond the Jordan is usually the east side. Radak says 'westward' means the western strip of that eastern land, the edge nearest the Jordan. Metzudat David also places it on the side facing the Land of Israel.

sources.quote: קצת הארץ אשר מעבר לירדן, הקצה שהוא לצד מערב לארץ ההיא לצד הירדן
sources.says: Radak says it is part of the land beyond the Jordan: its western edge, beside the Jordan.

sources.quote: בעבר הירדן בחלק המערבי ממנו הפונה מול ארץ ישראל
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the western part of the land beyond the Jordan, facing the Land of Israel.

27:4.headline: Is the 'and' part of Mikloth's name?
27:4.body: The name is written ומקלות, starting with the letter that means 'and'. Metzudat Zion and Malbim say that letter belongs to the name. Ralbag thinks it is extra, and that Mikloth led the division after Dodai.

sources.quote: כן שמו בוי״ו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says his name is spelled with the vav.

sources.quote: ווא"ו ומקלות הוא מן השם
sources.says: Malbim says Mikloth helped lead the division and the vav is part of the name.

sources.quote: אחשוב כי וא"ו של ומקלות נוספת
sources.says: Ralbag thinks the vav is extra, and Mikloth was the commander after Dodai.

27:5.headline: Was Benaiah's father the high priest?
27:5.body: The verse calls Yehoyada 'the priest, head'. Radak says he was the high priest. Rashi rejects this, since Zadok and Evyatar were the high priests, and reads 'head' as a leader.

sources.quote: יהוידע היה כהן גדול
sources.says: Radak says Yehoyada was high priest, as an earlier verse calls him leader of Aaron's house.

sources.quote: וְאֵינוֹ כֵּן, שֶׁהֲרֵי צָדוֹק וְאֶבְיָתָר הָיוּ כֹּהֲנִים גְּדוֹלִים
sources.says: Rashi says 'head' means a leader, and rejects the view that he was high priest because Zadok and Evyatar held that role.

27:6.headline: Hero of 'the thirty', or hero of the officers
27:6.body: Rashi reads השלשים as the famous band of thirty warriors listed earlier in the book. Metzudat Zion reads it as שלישים, officers, like Pharaoh's 'chosen officers' at the sea.

sources.quote: גִּבּוֹר הַשְּׁלֹשִׁים. כְּדִלְעֵיל
sources.says: Rashi points back to the earlier list where Benaiah is honored among the thirty.

sources.quote: שרים וממונים כמו ומבחר שלישיו
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means officers and appointed men, as in 'his chosen officers'.

27:18.headline: A brother of David missing from the family list
27:18.body: Samuel says Jesse had eight sons, but Chronicles lists only seven. A midrash says the eighth was this Elihu, a younger brother. Radak also allows that Elihu is one of the known brothers under a second name.

sources.quote: ולו שני שמות; או הוא אחר מלבד הנזכרים
sources.says: Radak says Elihu is either one of David's listed brothers with a second name, or another brother, as the midrash says.

sources.quote: ודעת חז"ל במדרש שהשמיני הוא אליהו הנזכר בין הנגידים שהקים דוד על יהודה
sources.says: Malbim brings the sages' view that the missing eighth son is the Elihu named here as leader of Judah.

sources.quote: לְפִיכָךְ לֹא מָנָה הַשְּׁמִינִי
sources.says: Rashi says the family list leaves out the eighth son, Elihu, and points to this verse.

27:33.headline: The king's friend was his best man
27:33.body: Rashi reads רע, friend, as שושבין, the groom's companion at a wedding. He backs this with the Targum on Samson's companion. Metzudat David says it means the man who kept the king company.

sources.quote: וְחוּשַׁי הָאַרְכִּי רֵעַ הַמֶּלֶךְ. שׁוֹשְׁבִינוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says 'the king's friend' means his groomsman, as the Targum renders Samson's companion.

sources.quote: הוא היה יושב בתמידות עם המלך להשתעשע עמו
sources.says: Metzudat David says he always sat with the king to keep him company.

27:33.headline: Hushai the Archite, who brought healing
27:33.body: A midrash hears ארוכה, healing, in Hushai's title הארכי. After the sin with Bathsheba, David asked him whether God would accept his repentance, and Hushai said yes.

sources.quote: אִם יְקַבְּלֵנוּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בִּתְשׁוּבָה, לָתֵת לוֹ אֲרוּכָה לְחֶטְאוֹ, וְאָמַר לוֹ כֵּן
sources.says: Rashi brings the midrash that David asked Hushai whether God would accept him and give healing for his sin, and Hushai said yes.

28:2.headline: Why mention that David stood on his feet?
28:2.body: Radak says the old king had already taken to his sickbed and pulled himself up to speak. Metzudat David says that although age had sapped his strength, he made himself stand to honor Israel's leaders.

sources.quote: התחזק וקם מהמשכב שהיה שם – כי כבר נפל למשכב
sources.says: Radak says David gathered his strength and rose from the sickbed he had already taken to.

sources.quote: כאומר עם כי תשש כחו בעבור הזקנה עכ״ז התחזק לעמוד על רגליו לכבוד שרי ישראל
sources.says: Metzudat David says that though old age had weakened him, he stood up in honor of Israel's leaders.

28:3.headline: Blood on his hands kept David from building the Temple
28:3.body: David was a man of war who had shed blood, so God did not let him build the Temple. Metzudat David compares this to the ban on lifting iron tools over the altar, because iron is used to make weapons.

sources.quote: ולכן מנעו לבנות וכאשר מנע מלהניף ברזל על המזבח על שעושים ממנו כלי רציחה
sources.says: Metzudat David says God kept him from building, just as iron may not be raised over the altar because killing tools are made from it.

28:9.headline: One heart, not two: why the verse says לב
28:9.body: Rashi notes the verse says לב, heart, not the longer לבב, which can hint at two hearts, so Solomon must serve with one undivided heart. In the next words, God searches all hearts, the plural לבבות fits, since it covers good and bad alike.

sources.quote: בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם לֹא נֶאֱמַר, שֶׁיְּהֵא מַשְׁמַע: שְׁנֵי לְבָבוֹת, אֶלָּא בְּלֵב שָׁלֵם
sources.says: Rashi says it does not say לבב שלם, which would suggest two hearts, but לב שלם, one whole heart.

sources.quote: כָּאן נוֹפֵל לוֹמַר לְבָבוֹת: כָּל לְבָבוֹת דּוֹרֵשׁ ה׳, בֵּין טוֹב וּבֵין רַע
sources.says: Rashi says here the plural fits, since God searches all hearts, good and bad.

28:9.headline: The heart forms thoughts the way hands form things
28:9.body: יצר means forming. Radak says the heart's work is called יצר because the heart forms ideas in thought, for good or for bad, and Rashi brings a midrash that God knows a person's thoughts before the person is even formed.

sources.quote: פעלת הלב תקרא "יצר", לפי שהלב פועל ויוצר במחשבה הענינים, הן לטוב הן לרע
sources.says: Radak says the heart's activity is called יצר because the heart forms ideas in thought, for good or bad.

sources.quote: קוֹדֶם שֶׁנּוֹצַר יְצִיר מֵבִין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מַה שֶּׁאָדָם עָתִיד לַחְשׁוֹב
sources.says: Rashi cites Bereshit Rabbah: before a creature is formed, God understands what a person will think.

sources.quote: יצר. הוא ענין פעולה
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says יצר means an action or work.

28:9.headline: Not just left behind, but cast off
28:9.body: The verse could have said God will leave you, but it says יזניחך. Rashi says this is harsher than leaving, the word used when God cast off his altar in Lamentations.

sources.quote: יַעַזְבְךָ אֵין כְּתִיב כָּאן, אֶלָּא יַזְנִיחֲךָ, שֶׁהוּא קָשֶׁה מִמֶּנּוּ
sources.says: Rashi says it does not say he will leave you but he will cast you off, which is harsher.

sources.quote: וכבר התבאר אצלי שפעל זנח מורה שעושה רושם בדבר המרוחק מאתו
sources.says: Malbim says the verb זנח means pushing something far away from oneself.

28:10.headline: A house for the sanctuary: Rashi says the Ark
28:10.body: Rashi says God cannot live in a house, since even the heavens cannot hold him. So a house for the מקדש means a house for the Ark, which the Torah calls the מקדש when the Kohathites carry it.

sources.quote: לֹא לִבְנוֹת לוֹ לָדוּר בּוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says it is not a house for God to live in.

sources.quote: לְצֹרֶךְ הָאָרוֹן שֶׁנִּקְרָא מִקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says it is for the Ark, which is called the מקדש.

28:11.headline: תבנית: a building's shape, a word never used of God
28:11.body: Maimonides cites this very verse to show that תבנית, from the root to build, means a thing's physical build and shape, like square or round. For that reason, he says, Hebrew never uses the word when describing God.

sources.quote: ומשמעותו מבנה הדבר ותכונתו, כלומר תבניתו, דוגמת הריבועיוּת והעיגוליוּת
sources.says: Maimonides says תבנית means the structure and form of a thing, such as being square or round.

sources.quote: ולכן אין העברית מחילה כלל את הביטויים הללו על תיאורים הקשורים באלוה
sources.says: Maimonides says that is why Hebrew never applies these terms to God.

sources.quote: תַּבְנִית הָאוּלָם. אָרְכּוֹ וְרָחְבּוֹ וְגָבְהוֹ
sources.says: Rashi says the תבנית of the hall is its length, width and height.

28:12.headline: In his spirit: a prophecy, or simply David's own plan?
28:12.body: Radak reads רוח as the spirit of prophecy, which showed David the Temple's design directly or through Samuel. Ralbag allows a plainer reading too: the plan David had in mind to build.

sources.quote: ברוח נבואה, כי על פי רוח הקדש ידע כל תבנית הבית, או על ידי עצמו או על ידי שמואל הנביא
sources.says: Radak says David knew the whole design by prophecy, either himself or through Samuel the prophet.

sources.quote: ברוח הקדש שהיתה עמו או ירצה בזה תבנית כל אשר היה עמו ברצונו לעשות מזה הבנין
sources.says: Ralbag says it means either the holy spirit that was with him, or the design he wished to make.

sources.quote: עוֹסְקִין הָיוּ בְּבִנְיָנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, הוּא בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi brings the Sages, who say David and Samuel worked together on the design of the Temple.

28:17.headline: Bowls named for wiping, the root of atonement
28:17.body: כפורים here are Temple bowls. Rashi and Radak say they are named for wiping, since the blood was wiped on them, and Rashi adds that every use of כפרה, atonement, means wiping clean.

sources.quote: כְּפוֹרֵי כְּלֵי שָׁרֵת, לְקַנֵּחַ בַּכֵּלִים הַדָּם מֵהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says they are Temple vessels used to wipe off blood.

sources.quote: וְכָל כַּפָּרָה – לְשׁוֹן קִנּוּחַ וְחִטּוּי הוּא
sources.says: Rashi says every use of כפרה means wiping and cleansing.

sources.quote: ונקראו כן על שם שמקנח בהם הסכין
sources.says: Radak says the bowls are named for wiping the knife on them.

28:18.headline: The cherubim called a chariot
28:18.body: The verse calls the golden cherubim a chariot, מרכבה. Rashi says the divine Presence rides on them, and Radak and Malbim link them to the chariot of living creatures that Ezekiel saw.

sources.quote: הֵם הַכְּרוּבִים שֶׁהַשְּׁכִינָה רוֹכֶבֶת עֲלֵיהֶם
sources.says: Rashi says these are the cherubim on which the divine Presence rides.

sources.quote: לתבנית מרכבת חיות הקדש, כי בהם פני הכרוב
sources.says: Radak says it is the pattern of the chariot of holy creatures, which have a cherub's face.

sources.quote: שהכרובים היו ציור למרכבת ה' ושכינת עזו כמו שראה יחזקאל
sources.says: Malbim says the cherubim pictured God's chariot as Ezekiel saw it.

28:19.headline: A Temple plan in writing, drawn from the Torah
28:19.body: David hands Solomon the whole plan in writing, from the hand of God. Rashi says Samuel worked out the measurements from the Torah by holy inspiration, for example the Temple Mount's 500 by 500 cubits from the size of the Tabernacle courtyard.

sources.quote: הַכֹּל בִּכְתָב סִדֵּר לוֹ, סְכוּם מִשְׁקָל וּמִשְׁקָל שֶׁל כָּל כְּלִי וּכְלִי
sources.says: Rashi says Samuel set out everything in writing, including the weight of each vessel.

sources.quote: וְהַכֹּל דָּרַשׁ שְׁמוּאֵל מִן הַתּוֹרָה בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says Samuel derived it all from the Torah by holy inspiration.

sources.quote: שיד ה' בא על השגת הנבואה
sources.says: Malbim says the hand of God refers to prophecy.

29:2.headline: Stones the color of eye paint
29:2.body: פוך is the dark paint used around the eyes, kohl. Radak and Metzudat Zion say these were precious stones that were kohl-colored, or made of kohl itself.

sources.quote: אבני יקר ומראיהם כעין הפוך והוא הכחול
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says these are precious stones that look like פוך, which is kohl.

sources.quote: וה"פוך" הוא הכחול; ואפשר שהיו אבני כחול, או אבנים יקרות עינם כעין הכחול
sources.says: Radak says פוך is kohl, so these were either stones of kohl or precious stones the color of kohl.

29:2.headline: Stones for "filling": why gems are called מלואים
29:2.body: Metzudat David says jewels are called מלואים, "fillings", because they fill the hollow cut into the setting to hold them.

sources.quote: כן יקראו אבני יקר ע״ש שממלאים את הגומא העשוי במשבצות להושיב בו האבן
sources.says: Metzudat David says precious stones are called this because they fill the hollow made in the setting to seat the stone.

29:2.headline: Embroidered cloth, or stones sewn into embroidery?
29:2.body: The verse lists רקמה, "embroidery", among stones. Radak and Metzudat Zion read it as embroidered cloth. Ralbag reads "embroidery stones": stones with holes that an embroiderer sews into a garment.

sources.quote: פי': בגדי רקמה ואבני פוך
sources.says: Radak says it means embroidered garments and kohl stones.

sources.quote: יריעות מרוקמות במיני צבעונין
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means sheets embroidered in many colors.

sources.quote: ידמה שהיו שם אבנים נקובים ישימם הרוקם בבגדים אשר יעשה והם נקראים אבני רקמה
sources.says: Ralbag says there seem to have been pierced stones that the embroiderer set into garments, called embroidery stones.

29:4.headline: The sages read this "silver" as gold that shamed all gold
29:4.body: The Temple walls were covered in gold, not silver. Radak says "to coat the walls" goes back to the gold. He also brings the sages' reading: this "silver" (כסף) was gold so fine it made all other gold pale (מכסף).

sources.quote: אלא למה קורין אותו כסף? שהיה מכסף כל בעלי זהבים
sources.says: Radak quotes the sages: why is it called silver? Because it put all owners of gold to shame.

sources.quote: ורז״ל אמרו שהכסף האמור כאן ר״ל זהב טוב המכסיף כל הזהבים
sources.says: Metzudat David says the sages read this silver as fine gold that shamed all other gold.

29:5.headline: "To fill his hand": the old phrase for starting a service
29:5.body: למלאות ידו means "to fill his hand". Rashi and Metzudat Zion say it is the phrase used for the priests' first service, "fill the hand of Aaron". Here it means to begin by giving a gift.

sources.quote: דֻּגְמַת ״וּמִלֵּאתָ יַד אַהֲרֹן וְיַד בָּנָיו״
sources.says: Rashi compares "you shall fill the hand of Aaron and his sons", which the Targum renders as bringing an offering.

sources.quote: למלאות. ענין חנוך כמו ומלאת יד אהרן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means a dedication, as in "fill the hand of Aaron".

29:9.headline: A "whole heart": one heart, not two
29:9.body: Rashi explains בלב שלם, "with a whole heart". Some people give against their will, or because they are ashamed in front of others. Rashi calls that "two hearts". These people gave with one heart.

sources.quote: בְּלֵב אֶחָד נָתְנוּ בִּרְצוֹן נַפְשָׁם, וְלֹא בִּשְׁנֵי לְבָבוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says they gave with one heart, willingly, not with two hearts.

sources.quote: וְהוּא נִקְרָא שְׁנֵי לְבָבוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says one who gives unwillingly or from shame is called "two hearts".

29:10.headline: "From world to world": forever, or this world and the next?
29:10.body: מעולם ועד עולם usually means "forever". Metzudat David and the Targum read עולם as "world": from this world to the world to come.

sources.quote: מהעה״ז עד העוה״ב
sources.says: Metzudat David says it means from this world to the world to come.

sources.quote: מִן עַלְמָא הָדֵין וְעַד עָלְמָא דְאָתֵי
sources.says: The Targum renders it "from this world to the world to come".

29:11.headline: "Yours is the greatness": the greatness is the Temple
29:11.body: This line is famous as praise of God. Rashi reads it in its setting: the "greatness" is the Temple, which is called by that word. David thanks God for the wealth to build it.

sources.quote: לְבִנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ שֶׁנִּקְרָא גְּדֻלָּה, אַתָּה נָתַתָּ לִי כָּל הַגְּדֻלָּה הַזֹּאת
sources.says: Rashi says the Temple building is called greatness, and God gave David all this greatness.

sources.quote: וְגַם לְשׁוֹן גְּדֻלָּה נוֹפֵל עַל בִּנְיַן בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says the word greatness is also used of building the Temple.

29:11.headline: נצח: victory, or eternity?
29:11.body: Rashi and Metzudat Zion read נצח as "victory": God let David win and take spoils for the Temple. Malbim reads it as eternity, a time above our time.

sources.quote: שֶׁנָּתַן לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִצָּחוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says God gave him victory.

sources.quote: והנצח. מל׳ נצחון
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says the word comes from victory.

sources.quote: ששם נצח מובדל משם עולם במה שמורה על זמן הנצחי של הרוחנים שהוא למעלה מן הזמן הידוע לנו
sources.says: Malbim says נצח differs from עולם: it means the eternal time of the spiritual world, above the time we know.

29:12.headline: "Honor" here means money
29:12.body: כבוד usually means honor. Rashi says here it means wealth, as when Laban's sons said Jacob took "all this כבוד" from their father.

sources.quote: וְהַכָּבוֹד נוֹפֵל עַל הָעֹשֶׁר
sources.says: Rashi says the word honor is used here for wealth.

sources.quote: וּמֵאֲשֶׁר לְאָבִינוּ עָשָׂה אֵת כָּל הַכָּבוֹד הַזֶּה
sources.says: Rashi compares "from what was our father's he made all this wealth" in Genesis 31.

29:22.headline: נגיד, "leader", heard as "the one who draws them along"
29:22.body: Rashi ties נגיד to the Aramaic נגידו, the Targum's word for "draw out". A leader is one who goes out and comes in before the people and leads them.

sources.quote: מִלְּשׁוֹן ״נְגִידוּ״ (תרגום אונקלוס), תַּרְגּוּם שֶׁל ״מִשְׁכוּ״
sources.says: Rashi says the word comes from נגידו, the Aramaic for "draw out".

29:23.headline: Solomon sat on "the throne of the Lord"
29:23.body: Rashi says the throne is called God's because God gives it to whom He wishes. He adds a midrash: Solomon was the fifteenth generation from Abraham, so his throne was full like the moon on the fifteenth of the month.

sources.quote: שֶׁהַכִּסֵּא שֶׁל ה׳ הוּא לְהַמְלִיךְ עָלָיו מִי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה
sources.says: Rashi says the throne is the Lord's, to set on it whomever He wants.

sources.quote: כִּסְאוֹ הָיָה מָלֵא, כְּמוֹ הַלְּבָנָה בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בַּחֹדֶשׁ
sources.says: Rashi says his throne was full, like the moon on the fifteenth of the month.

29:24.headline: "They gave a hand under Solomon": a pledge of loyalty
29:24.body: Rashi says "giving a hand" means a handshake of loyalty. Malbim says it means to submit. Ibn Ezra says it was a custom to put one's hands under the king's hand, as Solomon's brothers did.

sources.quote: אֱמוּנָה, תָּקְעוּ כַף לִשְׁלֹמֹה לְעָבְדוֹ בְּלֵבָב שָׁלֵם
sources.says: Rashi says it means faith: they struck hands with Solomon to serve him wholeheartedly.

sources.quote: להכנע תחתיו
sources.says: Malbim says it means to submit beneath him.

sources.quote: ומנהג גוים בעולם לשום ידיהם תחת יד המלך כאחי שלמה
sources.says: Ibn Ezra says it was a custom of nations to put their hands under the king's hand, like Solomon's brothers.

29:25.headline: The "majesty" of kingship: charm, fear, or inner worth?
29:25.body: Rashi says הוד מלכות is the grace of a king: everyone said "this one is fit". Radak says the world feared him. Malbim says הוד is an inner quality of the soul, unlike הדר, outward splendor.

sources.quote: נָתַן עָלָיו חֵן מַלְכוּת
sources.says: Rashi says God gave him the grace of kingship.

sources.quote: שהיו יראים כל העולם ממנו ומנשאים אותו
sources.says: Radak says the whole world feared him and raised him up.

sources.quote: וההוד הוא ענין פנימי נפשיי
sources.says: Malbim says הוד is an inner quality of the soul.

4:3.headline: The sages say this sister was Samson's mother
4:3.body: The verse names one sister, הצללפוני. Malbim brings the sages' tradition that she was the mother of Samson.

sources.quote: ולקבלת חז"ל היתה אמו של שמשון
sources.says: Malbim says that by the sages' tradition she was Samson's mother.

sources.quote: או היו בעלות השם בדורם ונשים חשובות – לכך הזכירם
sources.says: Radak says sisters are named when they were well known and important women in their day.

4:9.headline: His name is the word for pain, with letters swapped
4:9.body: His mother named him יעבץ because she bore him in pain, עצב. The name swaps two letters of that word, and Radak says Hebrew names often bend their source like this.

sources.quote: ולזכרון קראה את בנה יעבץ בהפוך אותיות מעצב כאלו תאמר שיהפך העצב לשמחה
sources.says: Metzudat David says she named him with the letters of עצב turned around, as if to say the pain would turn into joy.

sources.quote: אע"פ שהוא הפוך אל הענין, כי היה לו לומר לפי הענין "יעצב", אינם מקפידים העברים על זה
sources.says: Radak says that by its meaning the name should be יעצב, but Hebrew speakers did not insist on this, as with the names נח and קין.

4:10.headline: Enlarge my border: more land, or more students?
4:10.body: Rashi reads גבולי, my border, as his share of land. Malbim, following the sages, reads it as widening his reach in wisdom and students.

sources.quote: וְהִרְבִּיתָ אֶת גְּבוּלִי. בַּנַּחֲלוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it means more land holdings.

sources.quote: ירבה גבולו בחכמה, שזה היה הגבול שגבל לו, וכמ"ש חז"ל (תמורה טז א) והרבית את גבולי בתלמידים
sources.says: Malbim says it means his border in wisdom, and cites the sages who read it as more students.

4:15.headline: Is the "and" part of the name?
4:15.body: וקנז looks like "and Kenaz", but Rashi and Radak say the vav is part of the man's name. Ralbag reads it without the vav: the son of Elah was Kenaz.

sources.quote: כָּךְ הָיָה שְׁמוֹ: וּקְנַז
sources.says: Rashi says that was his name: וקנז.

sources.quote: כך היה שמו: "וקנז", בוי"ו
sources.says: Radak says his name was וקנז, with the vav.

sources.quote: ובני אלה וקנז. ר"ל ובני אלה קנז
sources.says: Ralbag reads it as "and the son of Elah was Kenaz".

4:17.headline: "She conceived": why not "she gave birth"?
4:17.body: Radak says ותהר, she conceived, here simply means she gave birth. Malbim says the verse chose this word because she carried all three sons at once.

sources.quote: ופרוש "ותהר" כמו "ותלד
sources.says: Radak says ותהר here means the same as ותלד, she gave birth.

sources.quote: ר"ל שהרתה כולם כאחד שלשה בכרס אחת, לכן אמר ותהר ולא אמר ותלד
sources.says: Malbim says she conceived all three in one pregnancy, which is why it says ותהר and not ותלד.

4:17.headline: This Miriam is a man
4:17.body: We know מרים as Moses' sister, but Radak says this Miriam is a son. He notes that many Hebrew names were used for both men and women.

sources.quote: מרים. בן הוא, כמו האחרים; כי הרבה נמצאים בשם אחד זכר ונקבה
sources.says: Radak says this Miriam is a son like the others, since many names are used for both males and females.

sources.quote: וילדה את מרים והוא שם איש
sources.says: Metzudat David says Miriam here is a man's name.

4:18.headline: "His Judean wife", or a woman named Hayehudiyah?
4:18.body: Radak reads היהדיה as "the Judean woman", which shows the other wife was not from Judah: she was Pharaoh's daughter. Malbim reads it as the third wife's name.

sources.quote: מכלל שהראשונה שהזכיר לא היתה יהודיה; והיא בתיה בת פרעה
sources.says: Radak says this implies the first wife was not Judean, and she was Bitya, Pharaoh's daughter.

sources.quote: אשה השלישית של כלב ששמה היהדיה
sources.says: Malbim says this was Caleb's third wife, and her name was היהדיה.

4:18.headline: "She bore him": the sages read "she raised him"
4:18.body: The plain sense is that she gave birth. Radak reports that the sages read these names as names of Moses, and read ילדה as raised, since he was like a son to her.

sources.quote: ודרשו כל אלה השמות – "ירד" ו"אבי גדור" ו"חבר" – כלם על משה רבנו; ואמ' "ילדה" כמו "גדלה", שהיה לה כבן
sources.says: Radak reports that the sages read these names as Moses, and read ילדה as גדלה, she raised him, because he was like her son.

4:18.headline: Mered is Caleb, who rebelled against the spies
4:18.body: Rashi, following the sages, says מרד is another name for Caleb. He was called this because he rebelled, מרד, against the spies' plan.

sources.quote: כָּלֵב הוּא מֶרֶד, שֶׁמָּרַד בַּעֲצַת מְרַגְּלִים
sources.says: Rashi says Caleb is Mered, because he rebelled against the spies' advice.

sources.quote: ולמה נקרא שמו "מרד"? שמרד בעצת מרגלים
sources.says: Radak brings the sages' reading that Mered is Caleb, named for rebelling against the spies.

4:22.headline: The sages find Naomi's sons in this list
4:22.body: Rashi says the sages identify יואש and שרף with מחלון and כליון, the sons of Naomi in the book of Ruth. Ralbag says they may have had two names each.

sources.quote: זֶה ״מַחְלוֹן וְכִלְיוֹן
sources.says: Rashi says the sages identify them as Machlon and Kilyon.

sources.quote: ואפשר עוד שהיו אלו מחלון וכליון והיו להם שני שמות
sources.says: Ralbag says it is also possible these were Machlon and Kilyon, who had two names.

4:22.headline: Ruled over Moab, or married into Moab?
4:22.body: בעלו comes from בעל, master or husband. Metzudat David says they fought Moab and ruled it, while Rashi, following the sages, says they married Moabite women.

sources.quote: אשר נלחמו עם מואב והיו אדונים להם
sources.says: Metzudat David says they fought Moab and became its masters.

sources.quote: שֶׁלָּקְחוּ נָשִׁים מוֹאֲבִיּוֹת
sources.says: Rashi says it means they took Moabite wives.

4:22.headline: A man's name, or "those who lived in Bethlehem"?
4:22.body: The sages read וישבי לחם as people from Bethlehem. Radak and Metzudat David, reading plainly, take it as one man's name.

sources.quote: וישבי לחם שהיו מבית לחם יהודה
sources.says: Radak reports the sages' reading: they were from Bethlehem in Judah.

sources.quote: ו"ישבי לחם" גם כן שם אחד מבניו
sources.says: Radak says that in the plain sense ישבי לחם is the name of one of his sons.

sources.quote: וישבי לחם. כן שם איש
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is a man's name.

4:22.headline: "The records are ancient", or "handed down"?
4:22.body: עתיקים can mean old, or copied and passed on. Metzudat Zion takes it as old, while Radak and Malbim also read it as handed down or copied.

sources.quote: עתיקים. ענין יושן
sources.says: Metzudat Zion says it means old.

sources.quote: הדברים הם ידועים בקבלה ובמסרה ונעתקים איש מפי איש
sources.says: Radak says these things were known by tradition and passed on from one person to the next.

sources.quote: ספור זה הוא ספור ישן עתיק ימים שהיה להם קבלה עתיקה, או ר"ל שפרטי המעשה נעתקו על ספר מיוחד
sources.says: Malbim says it is either a very old story, or that the details were copied into a special book.

4:23.headline: Planters, or people from a place called Netaim?
4:23.body: Rashi says they tended the king's plantings. Malbim adds that נטעים and גדרה may be the names of the places where they lived.

sources.quote: שֶׁהָיוּ עוֹסְקִים בִּנְטִיעוֹת שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ
sources.says: Rashi says they worked in the king's plantings.

sources.quote: גם יל"פ שהמקומות שישבו שם היו קרוים נטעים וגדרה
sources.says: Malbim says it can also be read as the names of the places where they lived.

4:33.headline: A word for family trees, used here for towns
4:33.body: יחש usually means a family tree, telling whose son a man is. Metzudat David and Radak say it is borrowed here to tell whose towns these were, while Malbim says the families were named after their towns.

sources.quote: ועם כי עיקר שם יחוס הונח על גלוי משפחת האיש לדעת מבני מי הוא הנה הושאל על הגלות העיר לדעת של מי הוא
sources.says: Metzudat David says יחוס first meant showing a man's family, and is borrowed here to show whose a town is.

sources.quote: ואיננו רחוק בלשון לזכור "יחש" בענין הערים
sources.says: Radak says it is not strange for the language to use יחש about towns.

sources.quote: שראשי המשפחות התיחשו אחר הערים
sources.says: Malbim says the heads of families took their family names from the towns.

4:41.headline: The Meunites, or their dwellings?
4:41.body: Metzudat David and Malbim take המעונים as the name of a people. Radak and Ralbag read it as from מעון, a dwelling: the buildings where the shepherds lived.

sources.quote: המעונים. שם אומה מעון
sources.says: Metzudat David says it is the name of a nation, Maon.

sources.quote: ואת המעונים. שם אומה נזכרה
sources.says: Malbim says it is the name of a nation mentioned elsewhere.

sources.quote: והוא קבוץ מן "מעוֹן" שהוא מקום הדירה
sources.says: Radak says it is the plural of מעון, a place to live.

sources.quote: והרצון בו המקומות הבנוים אשר שם שהיו יושבים שם רועים
sources.says: Ralbag says it means the buildings there where shepherds lived.
